_sourceRefs: Stedi (stedi.com/edi/edi/hipaa/transaction-set/270-B1) — the HIPAA-specific (005010X279A1) 270 Eligibility, Coverage or Benefit Inquiry transaction set, EDI X12 Phase 3. PyX12's own free map repo (azoner/pyx12/pyx12/map) was checked first and confirmed to only ship a 4010/X092 map for 270/271 (no 5010/X279 file exists there) — sourced instead from Stedi's own HIPAA-specific guide page, verified distinct from Stedi's generic (non-HIPAA) 005010/270 page, which the fetch itself flagged as not the HIPAA transaction when asked for lettered-loop/HL03 detail.

HL03 trigger discriminators (20/21/22/23) reuse the exact X12LoopDef.TriggerDiscriminator mechanism already proven for 837P/837I's own 2000A/B/C ancestor-vs-descendant disambiguation (see edi/loop_engine.go's matchLoops two-pass algorithm) — zero new engine code, pure schema data.

FunctionalIdentifierCode 'HS' (Health Care Eligibility Benefit Inquiry) and VersionReleaseIndustryCode '005010X279A1' are the well-known, standard values for this transaction — not yet cross-checked against one live real-world sample file the way 835's own GS01/GS08 values were; flag for confirmation the first time a real 270 sample is available.

Named, deliberate simplifications (matching 837's own 'core fields, not exhaustive' precedent): loop 2117 (LQ) omitted — it appeared only on Stedi's generic, explicitly-non-HIPAA 270 page, never confirmed on the HIPAA-specific 270-B1 page, too low-confidence to model as real; re-confirmed absent by a direct re-fetch of 270-B1 during a later polish pass (no 2117/LQ mentioned anywhere on that page). MPI (Military Personnel Information) omitted from 2100A-D — a narrow, rarely-populated field. TRN (2000C/2000D) reuses the existing globally-shared TRN.json, whose maxUse stays '1' (unchanged, to avoid regressing 835/837's own already-proven TRN usage as a single header segment) even though 270/271 can technically carry up to 3 TRN occurrences per HL instance — a real trading partner sending more than one TRN per subscriber/dependent loop would only have the first captured; named, not attempted.

Loop 2120 (LS/LE-wrapped Related Entity) does NOT exist in 270 at all — confirmed by a direct re-fetch of Stedi's 270-B1 page during the same later polish pass that added 2120C/2120D to 271.json: the page's detail section ends at 2110C/2110D, with no 2120/LS/LE mentioned anywhere. This is a real, request-vs-response spec asymmetry (271 needs to be able to name a related entity for a benefit it found; 270 has nothing yet to relate one to), not an oversight or a remaining gap on this transaction set.
